Jonas — thanks for the note.

Short background: Acme's procurement/legal team is pushing for a carve-out that would preserve recoverability of consequential and special damages where the breach causes measurable downstream losses to our customers (lost revenue, contract penalties passed downstream). This is not targeted at ordinary negligence; it is intended for scenarios where Redwood's product failure directly causes material downstream financial harm.

Practical ask: our counsel is proposing one-way language limited to (i) third-party claims resulting from data exfiltration or regulatory fines, and (ii) documented direct downstream revenue loss caused by a critical service failure. For commercial comfort, Acme is prepared to accept a narrow list of exclusions and a negotiated cap that sits above the standard MSA cap for those categories.

Attached is our markup (Acme_redline.docx) — the flagged language is in section 9. We are flexible on mutuality if we can get explicit carve-outs for the two categories above.

If you prefer, we can jump on a call; Ben is available at 3pm ET today.

Team —

I reviewed Acme's markup and the commercial note from Maria. We should avoid a blanket one-way carve-out. That said, Acme's commercial drivers are understandable: (a) regulatory fines stemming from data incidents, and (b) quantifiable downstream revenue loss tied to a critical outage. We can bridge this with narrow, enumerated exceptions plus mutuality and well-scoped definitions.

Suggested compromise (high level):
- Keep the overall liability cap in the MSA (12 months fees) for most categories.
- Preserve mutual exclusion of consequential, special, incidental and punitive damages.
- Add an explicit carve-out (mutual) limited to the following categories:
  1) Liability for claims arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence;
  2) IP infringement indemnity obligations;
  3) Payment obligations; and
  4) Damages directly resulting from an incident causing regulated data exposure (subject to proof and root-cause analysis).

If Acme insists on recoverability for downstream revenue loss, we should require: (i) a causal link showing Redwood's failure was the proximate cause, (ii) objective documentation (customer chargebacks/penalty notices), and (iii) a sub-cap (e.g., 3x the standard cap or a fixed dollar band) — plus a mutual fallback allowing Redwood to pursue mitigation credits (service credits, remediation scope).

Proposed draft clause (for negotiation):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other under this agreement for incidental, special, punitive or consequential damages, except that this exclusion shall not apply to: (a) liability resulting from gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) claims for infringement of intellectual property; (c) payment obligations; and (d) damages, to the extent directly caused by an event of regulated data exposure confirmed by root-cause analysis and documented third-party fines or customer penalties, subject to a sub-cap of [USD X] and the mitigation obligations in Section Y."

Action items:
- Jonas: confirm commercial appetite for sub-cap approach (Acme may push for higher multiple).
- Karthik: can your team outline how we would demonstrate root cause and impact metrics in case of a data incident? That will determine the practicality of the carve-out.
- Marissa: if you agree, I'll tidy this into a tracked-change draft to send back.

Laura
